paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: Proverbs 12 is about two roads, and the road you're on is built out of small everyday choices. Solomon says, "Whoever loves discipline loves knowledge, but he who hates correction is stupid" (Proverbs 12:1). That means the wise baker lets correction in, even when it stings, and listens to counsel instead of trusting a gut that's sure it's right (Proverbs 12:15). Nobody enjoys hearing "you missed a spot," but I'd rather hear it from a friend than find out from the whole batch.

Then look at how much of this chapter lands on your mouth and your hands. "Truthful lips endure forever, but a lying tongue lasts only a moment" (Proverbs 12:19). "Speaking rashly is like a piercing sword, but the tongue of the wise brings healing" (Proverbs 12:18), and "Anxiety weighs down the heart of a man, but a good word cheers it up" (Proverbs 12:25). So your words can wound or they can lift somebody, and your honest work counts too, because "The hand of the diligent will rule, but laziness ends in forced labor" (Proverbs 12:24). It's not glamorous, but the one who keeps working the land is the one who EATS (Proverbs 12:11).

And here's why it matters, baker. Solomon isn't handing out rules just to keep you busy. He ends with this promise: "There is life in the path of righteousness, but another path leads to death" (Proverbs 12:28). Pick the road of honest lips, humble ears and faithful hands, and you're walking toward life, one small step at a time.
